content: Bisacodyl is a laxative that is prescribed for short-term use to treat constipation. It is also used to empty the bowels before surgical procedures or diagnostic tests, such as X-rays involving barium enemas. This medication is available both with and without a prescription. In some cases, it may be prescribed for other uses; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Bisacodyl is available in several forms: as an oral tablet, a rectal suppository, or an enema. The oral tablets are typically taken the evening before a bowel movement is desired, while the suppositories or enemas are used at the time a bowel movement is needed. Follow the instructions on the package or your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. For bowel preparation before surgery or an examination, bisacodyl is usually taken orally the night before and rectally the morning of the procedure. Oral tablets generally produce a bowel movement within 6 to 8 hours, suppositories within 15 to 60 minutes, and enemas within 3 to 5 minutes. Do not take bisacodyl more than once a day or for longer than one week without consulting your doctor. Swallow the tablets whole; do not crush or chew them. Avoid taking the tablets within one hour of consuming milk or antacids. If you are preparing for a barium enema, do not eat after taking the tablets. Use bisacodyl exactly as directed, and do not take more or less than prescribed. Prolonged or frequent use of bisacodyl can lead to dependency on laxatives and impair the normal function of your bowels. If you do not have a bowel movement or experience rectal bleeding after using this medication as directed for one week, contact your doctor. Do not administer bisacodyl to children under 10 years of age unless directed by a doctor. If you are using a bisacodyl suppository, follow these steps: 1. Remove the wrapper. 2. Moisten the tip of the suppository with lukewarm water. 3. Lie on your left side and bring your right knee to your chest. (Left-handed individuals should lie on their right side and raise their left knee.) 4. Using your finger, insert the suppository high into the rectum. Hold it in place for a few moments and try to retain it for as long as possible. 5. Wash your hands thoroughly. If you are using a bisacodyl enema, follow these steps: 1. Shake the enema bottle well. 2. Remove the protective shield from the tip. 3. Lie on your left side and bring your right knee to your chest. (Left-handed individuals should lie on their right side and raise their left knee.) 4. Gently insert the enema bottle tip into the rectum, pointing it toward the navel. 5. Squeeze the bottle gently until nearly all the medication is expelled. 6. Remove the enema bottle and retain the contents in the rectum for as long as possible. 7. Wash your hands thoroughly. Before taking bisacodyl, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to bisacodyl, aspirin, tartrazine (a yellow dye found in some processed foods and medications, including bisacodyl), or any other drugs. Additionally, disclose all prescription and nonprescription medications you are currently taking. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking bisacodyl, contact your doctor. If you forget a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Bisacodyl may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they are severe or persistent: Stomach cramps Upset stomach Diarrhea Irritation or burning in the rectum (from suppositories) Faintness Stomach and intestinal irritation Store bisacodyl in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of expired or unneeded medication properly; consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. Keep all appointments with your doctor. Do not share this medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist. Bisacodyl is sold under various brand names, including: Alophen® Pills Bisac-Evac® Bisacodyl Uniserts® Carter's Little Pills® Correctol® Caplets® Correctol® Tablets Dulcolax® Dulcolax® Bowel Prep Kit Evac-Q-Kwik® Kit Feen-A-Mint® Fleet® Bisacodyl Fleet® Bisacodyl Enema Fleet® Prep Kit No. 1 Fleet® Prep Kit No. 2
